questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the $S_N2$ reaction of an alkyl halide are correct?
(i) It occurs in a single step and no intermediate is formed.
(ii) In the transition state, the carbon under attack is simultaneously bonded to five atoms.
(iii) In the transition state for $CH_3Cl + OH^-$, the three C–H bonds lie in one plane.
(iv) Its reactivity order is tertiary > secondary > primary halide.
(v) An optically active halide reacts with retention of configuration.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: bond making and bond breaking occur simultaneously.
(ii) Correct: the transition state is pentacoordinate and cannot be isolated.
(iii) Correct: the three C–H bonds flatten into one plane as the nucleophile approaches.
(iv) Incorrect: steric hindrance gives the order $CH_3$ > 1° > 2° > 3°.
(v) Incorrect: attack from the side opposite the leaving group causes inversion of configuration.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In chlorobenzene, chlorine withdraws electron density from the ring by its –I effect, so the ring is deactivated compared with benzene.
Statement II: Electrophilic substitution in chlorobenzene is faster than in benzene because the +R effect of chlorine outweighs its –I effect.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: the –I effect of Cl withdraws electrons, so the ring is somewhat deactivated.
Statement II is incorrect: the inductive effect is stronger than resonance. Electrophilic substitution in haloarenes is therefore slower and needs more drastic conditions than in benzene.
The +R effect only controls orientation. It makes deactivation smaller at the ortho and para positions.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: Haloalkanes, although polar, are only very slightly soluble in water.
Statement II: The energy released when haloalkane–water attractions form is less than the energy needed to break the hydrogen bonds between water molecules and the attractions between haloalkane molecules.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT describes haloalkanes as very slightly soluble in water.
Statement II is correct. To dissolve a haloalkane, energy must be spent to break the strong hydrogen bonds in water and the attractions between haloalkane molecules. The new haloalkane–water attractions are weaker, so less energy is released.
This energy deficit is the reason for the low solubility. Statement II therefore correctly explains Statement I.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A mixture of bromoethane and bromobenzene is treated with sodium in dry ether to prepare ethylbenzene. Apart from ethylbenzene, which pair of hydrocarbons is also expected to form as by-products?
questions.explanation:
The cross-coupling of an alkyl halide with an aryl halide (Wurtz–Fittig reaction) gives ethylbenzene, $C_6H_5C_2H_5$.
In the same flask, two ethyl groups can also couple with each other (a Wurtz-type reaction): $C_2H_5$–$C_2H_5$ = n-butane.
Two phenyl groups can likewise couple (a Fittig-type reaction): $C_6H_5$–$C_6H_5$ = biphenyl.
Toluene and propane would need methyl groups, and styrene would need a C=C bond; none of these can arise from these halides.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Arrange the following isomeric bromides in increasing order of boiling point:
(P) 1-Bromobutane
(Q) 2-Bromobutane
(R) 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane
questions.explanation:
All three isomers have the same molecular mass, so only their shape decides the boiling point.
More branching makes a molecule more compact. This reduces its surface area of contact and weakens the van der Waals forces.
2-Bromo-2-methylpropane (tertiary) is the most branched, so it has the lowest boiling point. 2-Bromobutane comes next. The straight-chain 1-bromobutane has the highest boiling point.
The increasing order is R < Q < P.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following molecules is achiral?
questions.explanation:
In propan-2-ol, CH3CH(OH)CH3, the central carbon carries two identical CH3 groups, so it has no asymmetric carbon.
If its mirror image is rotated by 180°, it superimposes on the original. The molecule is therefore achiral.
Butan-2-ol, 2-chlorobutane and 2-bromopropanoic acid each have one carbon bearing four different groups. Each is chiral.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reactants with metal) with List-II (type of product).
List-I:
(P) $CH_3Br$ + Na, dry ether
(Q) $C_6H_5Br$ + $CH_3Br$ + Na, dry ether
(R) $C_6H_5Br$ + Na, dry ether
(S) $C_2H_5Br$ + Mg, dry ether
List-II:
(i) Biphenyl
(ii) Organometallic compound
(iii) Alkylarene (toluene)
(iv) Ethane
questions.explanation:
(P) The Wurtz reaction couples two methyl groups to give ethane: (iv).
(Q) The Wurtz–Fittig reaction joins an alkyl and an aryl halide with Na. The product is an alkylarene, $C_6H_5CH_3$: (iii).
(R) The Fittig reaction joins two aryl groups to give biphenyl: (i).
(S) Mg in dry ether forms the Grignard reagent $C_2H_5MgBr$, an organometallic compound: (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Optically active 2-bromobutane undergoes hydrolysis by the SN1 mechanism. How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) The carbocation formed is sp$^2$ hybridised and planar.
(ii) The carbocation intermediate is achiral.
(iii) Under the idealised picture, the product is a 50:50 mixture of molecules with retained and inverted configuration.
(iv) The product, (±)-butan-2-ol, is optically inactive.
(v) The rate of the reaction depends on the concentration of hydroxide ion.
(vi) The slowest step is the attack of the nucleophile on the carbocation.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: The carbocation formed in the slow step is sp$^2$ hybridised and planar.
(ii) Correct: Being planar, the carbocation is achiral.
(iii) Correct: The nucleophile can attack equally from either face of the plane, giving retained and inverted products.
(iv) Correct: The racemic product is (±)-butan-2-ol, which is optically inactive.
(v) Incorrect: SN1 is first order; the rate depends only on the concentration of alkyl halide.
(vi) Incorrect: The slow step is the ionisation of the C–Br bond, not the nucleophilic attack.
Correct statements = 4.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ethyl bromide is heated with silver nitrite ($AgNO_2$). What is the main organic product?
questions.explanation:
The nitrite group is an ambident nucleophile. It can bond through oxygen or through nitrogen.
In $AgNO_2$ (Ag–O–N=O), oxygen is bound to silver. This leaves the nitrogen lone pair free to attack the carbon.
Attack through N gives the nitroalkane $R-NO_2$, here nitroethane.
Ethyl nitrite is the product with $KNO_2$, where linkage is through O. Ethyl isocyanide comes from AgCN.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the following alkanes: ethane, propane, n-butane, 2-methylpropane, 2,3-dimethylbutane, n-hexane, 2-methylbutane.
How many of them can be obtained as the single product of a Wurtz reaction using only ONE alkyl halide (with Na in dry ether)?
questions.explanation:
A Wurtz reaction with a single halide RX joins two identical R groups, giving the symmetrical alkane R–R.
Alkanes that can be made this way:
Ethane comes from $CH_3X$.
n-Butane comes from $C_2H_5X$.
2,3-Dimethylbutane comes from isopropyl halide.
n-Hexane comes from n-propyl halide.
Alkanes that cannot be made this way, because they cannot be split into two identical halves:
Propane, which has an odd number of carbons.
2-Methylpropane.
2-Methylbutane.
So the total is 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many structurally different monochloro products (ignoring stereoisomers) can form on free radical monochlorination of methylcyclohexane?
questions.explanation:
The ring has a plane of symmetry through C-1, C-4 and the methyl group, so C-2 ≡ C-6 and C-3 ≡ C-5.
The distinct types of hydrogen are: (i) on the CH$_3$ group, (ii) on C-1, (iii) on C-2/C-6, (iv) on C-3/C-5, (v) on C-4.
Each type gives a different monochloride, so there are 5 structural isomers.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The hydrolysis of tert-butyl bromide by hydroxide ion follows first-order kinetics. If the concentration of $OH^-$ is doubled while the concentration of tert-butyl bromide is kept the same, the rate of the reaction will:
questions.explanation:
This is an $S_N1$ reaction. Its slow, rate-determining step is ionisation of the C–Br bond to form the tert-butyl carbocation.
$OH^-$ attacks only in the fast second step.
So rate = k[tert-butyl bromide], and the rate does not depend on $[OH^-]$.
Doubling $[OH^-]$ therefore leaves the rate unchanged.
"Double" would apply only to a second-order ($S_N2$) process.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match each observation in List-I with its best explanation in List-II.
List-I
(A) CH3I boils higher than CH3Cl
(B) 1,4-Dichlorobenzene melts higher than 1,2-dichlorobenzene
(C) 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane has the lowest b.p. among the isomeric C4H9Br bromides (1-bromobutane, 2-bromobutane, 2-bromo-2-methylpropane)
(D) Chloromethane boils higher than a hydrocarbon of comparable molecular mass
List-II
(i) Symmetrical molecules fit better into the crystal lattice
(ii) Compact, branched shape reduces intermolecular contact
(iii) Polar C–X bond adds dipole-dipole attraction
(iv) Larger size and mass of halogen strengthens van der Waals forces
questions.explanation:
(A) Iodine is much larger and heavier than chlorine, so the van der Waals forces are stronger. This matches (iv).
(B) The para isomer is symmetrical and packs better in the lattice, so it melts higher. This matches (i).
(C) The tertiary isomer is the most branched and compact, so its intermolecular forces are weakest. This matches (ii).
(D) The polar C–Cl bond adds dipole-dipole attraction, which a non-polar hydrocarbon lacks. This matches (iii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): 1,4-Dichlorobenzene melts at a much higher temperature than 1,2- and 1,3-dichlorobenzene.
Reason (R): The para isomer has a much higher boiling point than the ortho and meta isomers because its dipole-dipole attractions are stronger.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The para isomer is symmetrical, so its molecules pack better in the crystal lattice. More energy is then needed to melt it.
R is false for two reasons. First, the boiling points of the isomeric dichlorobenzenes are very nearly the same. Second, the para isomer is symmetrical, so its bond dipoles cancel and its net dipole moment is about zero. Its dipole-dipole attraction cannot be the strongest.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Using the densities CH2Cl2 = 1.336 g/mL and CCl4 = 1.595 g/mL, what volume of CCl4 has the same mass as 50.0 mL of CH2Cl2?
questions.explanation:
Given: V(CH2Cl2) = 50.0 mL, density of CH2Cl2 = 1.336 g/mL, density of CCl4 = 1.595 g/mL.
Formula: mass = density × volume, so V(CCl4) = mass / density of CCl4.
Substituting: mass = 50.0 × 1.336 = 66.8 g. Then V = 66.8 / 1.595 = 41.9 mL.
So the required volume of CCl4 is 41.9 mL. This is smaller than 50.0 mL because CCl4 has more Cl atoms and is denser.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: Benzyl chloride, $C_6H_5CH_2Cl$, is classified as an aryl halide because its halogen-bearing carbon is attached to a benzene ring.
Statement II: In vinylic halides, the halogen is bonded to an $sp^2$-hybridised carbon of a carbon–carbon double bond.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. In benzyl chloride, Cl is on an $sp^3$ $CH_2$ carbon that is attached to the ring, so it is a benzylic halide. An aryl halide needs the halogen directly on an $sp^2$ ring carbon, as in $C_6H_5Cl$.
Statement II is correct. A vinylic halide, such as $CH_2=CHCl$, has the halogen on an $sp^2$ carbon of a C=C.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Haloalkanes react with KCN to give alkyl cyanides (nitriles) as the main product.
Reason (R): KCN is predominantly ionic, and the free cyanide ion attacks mainly through carbon because a C–C bond is more stable than a C–N bond.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. R–X + KCN gives RCN, a nitrile.
R is true. KCN supplies free $CN^-$ ions in solution. Both C and N could donate a lone pair, but attack occurs mainly through C because the C–C bond formed is more stable.
R therefore explains A directly.
Contrast: AgCN is largely covalent, so nitrogen does the attacking and an isocyanide forms.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following compounds are chiral?
Butan-2-ol, propan-2-ol, 2-chlorobutane, bromochloroiodomethane, 2-bromopropanoic acid, 1-chlorobutane, 2-bromopropane
questions.explanation:
Butan-2-ol: chiral. C-2 carries H, OH, CH$_3$ and C$_2$H$_5$.
Propan-2-ol: achiral, because C-2 has two CH$_3$ groups.
2-Chlorobutane: chiral. C-2 carries H, Cl, CH$_3$ and C$_2$H$_5$.
BrClCHI: chiral. The carbon carries four different atoms.
2-Bromopropanoic acid: chiral. C-2 carries H, Br, CH$_3$ and COOH.
1-Chlorobutane and 2-bromopropane: achiral, as no carbon has four different groups.
Total chiral compounds = 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (scientist) with List-II (contribution):
List-I
(a) William Nicol
(b) Louis Pasteur
(c) Van't Hoff and Le Bel
(d) Hughes and Ingold
List-II
(i) Proposed the tetrahedral arrangement of four groups around carbon
(ii) Proposed the mechanism of the SN2 reaction
(iii) Developed the first prism that produced plane polarised light
(iv) Observed that crystals of certain compounds exist as mirror images
questions.explanation:
(a) Nicol developed the first prism giving plane polarised light, so (a)-(iii).
(b) Pasteur (1848) observed crystals existing as mirror images, so (b)-(iv).
(c) Van't Hoff and Le Bel (1874) proposed the tetrahedral arrangement of groups around carbon, so (c)-(i).
(d) Hughes and Ingold (1937) proposed the SN2 mechanism, so (d)-(ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorobenzene can be converted into phenol by nucleophilic replacement of chlorine by a hydroxyl group. Under which conditions is this conversion carried out?
options: Heating with aqueous NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm, followed by acidification
Warming with aqueous NaOH at 300 K and 1 atm
Heating with alcoholic KOH at 373 K
Shaking with concentrated HCl and anhydrous $ZnCl_2$ at room temperature
questions.explanation:
Aryl halides are very unreactive towards nucleophiles, so drastic conditions are needed.
NCERT: chlorobenzene gives phenol when heated with aqueous NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm, followed by acidification.
Mild warming with aqueous NaOH works for haloalkanes, not for chlorobenzene.
Alcoholic KOH is used for dehydrohalogenation of haloalkanes, and HCl/$ZnCl_2$ converts alcohols into alkyl chlorides.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: For the same alkyl group, the boiling points of alkyl halides follow the order RI > RBr > RCl > RF.
Statement II: Among isomeric haloalkanes, the boiling point increases as branching increases.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The size and mass of the halogen increase from F to I. So the van der Waals forces get stronger and the boiling point rises in the order RF < RCl < RBr < RI.
Statement II is incorrect. Branching makes the molecule more compact, which lowers the boiling point.
For example, 2-bromo-2-methylpropane has the lowest boiling point among its isomers.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the methyl halides CH$_3$F, CH$_3$Cl, CH$_3$Br and CH$_3$I:
(i) The C–X bond length increases from CH$_3$F to CH$_3$I.
(ii) The C–X bond enthalpy decreases from CH$_3$F to CH$_3$I.
(iii) CH$_3$F has the highest dipole moment, because fluorine is the most electronegative halogen.
(iv) CH$_3$I has the lowest dipole moment of the four.
How many of these statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: halogen size increases down the group, so the bond length goes 139 → 214 pm.
(ii) Correct: the bond enthalpy falls from 452 to 234 kJ/mol.
(iii) Incorrect: CH$_3$Cl has the highest dipole moment (1.860 D vs 1.847 D for CH$_3$F). The very short C–F bond offsets fluorine's higher electronegativity.
(iv) Correct: CH$_3$I has 1.636 D, the lowest of the four.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about nucleophilic substitution in haloalkanes is INCORRECT?
options: An SN2 reaction of an optically active alkyl halide gives a product with inverted configuration
The rate of an SN1 reaction depends only on the concentration of the alkyl halide
In the SN2 transition state, carbon is bonded to five atoms, and this species can be isolated because it is stabilised by the solvent
The carbocation formed in an SN1 reaction is sp2 hybridised and planar, so an optically active halide gives a racemic product
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: in SN2 the nucleophile attacks from the side opposite the leaving group, so the configuration is inverted.
(2) Correct: the slow first step, ionisation of R–X, decides the rate. So SN1 shows first-order kinetics.
(3) Incorrect: carbon is indeed partially bonded to five groups in the transition state. However, NCERT stresses that such structures are unstable and cannot be isolated.
(4) Correct: the nucleophile can attack the planar carbocation from either face, which gives a (±) mixture.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) $CCl_4$ is a non-polar molecule even though each C–Cl bond in it is polar.
(ii) $CH_2Cl_2$ has a higher dipole moment than $CHCl_3$.
(iii) The C–Cl bond enthalpy in $CH_3Cl$ is greater than the C–Br bond enthalpy in $CH_3Br$.
(iv) In $CHCl_3$ the bond dipoles cancel completely, so its dipole moment is zero.
(v) $CH_3Br$ has a higher dipole moment than $CH_3I$.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: in the symmetric tetrahedral $CCl_4$, the four bond dipoles cancel to give zero net dipole.
(ii) Correct: in $CH_2Cl_2$ the C–Cl dipoles reinforce strongly. In $CHCl_3$ they partly cancel, so its net moment is smaller.
(iii) Correct: the C–Cl bond enthalpy is 351 kJ/mol and the C–Br value is 293 kJ/mol.
(iv) Incorrect: $CHCl_3$ is not fully symmetric, so it has a net dipole.
(v) Correct: $CH_3Br$ has 1.830 D and $CH_3I$ has 1.636 D.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the sequence:
1-Bromobutane $\xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}}$ P $\xrightarrow{HBr}$ Q
Q is then treated separately with (a) alcoholic KOH, giving major product R, and (b) sodium in dry ether, giving S.
R and S are, respectively:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: β-elimination of 1-bromobutane gives P = but-1-ene. This is the only possibility.
Step 2: HBr adds by Markovnikov's rule, giving Q = 2-bromobutane, $CH_3CHBrCH_2CH_3$.
Step 3: Q has two kinds of β-H. By Zaitsev's rule, the more substituted alkene is major, so R = but-2-ene.
Step 4: The Wurtz reaction joins two sec-butyl groups. $CH_3CH_2CH(CH_3)–CH(CH_3)CH_2CH_3$ is 3,4-dimethylhexane, so S = 3,4-dimethylhexane.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A student treats an equimolar mixture of bromobenzene and bromoethane with sodium in dry ether to prepare ethylbenzene by the Wurtz–Fittig reaction. Like-groups can also couple with each other. Which of the following compounds is NOT expected in the product mixture?
questions.explanation:
Na couples any two of the organic groups present. Here the groups are phenyl and ethyl.
Phenyl + ethyl gives ethylbenzene, the Wurtz–Fittig product.
Phenyl + phenyl gives biphenyl, the Fittig-type side product.
Ethyl + ethyl gives n-butane, the Wurtz-type side product.
Toluene needs a methyl group attached to the ring, but no methyl halide is present. So toluene cannot form.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An aromatic primary amine A ($C_7H_9N$) has its $-NH_2$ and $-CH_3$ groups para to each other. A is dissolved in cold dilute HCl and treated with $NaNO_2$ to give B. One portion of B is mixed with CuBr to give C. Another portion of B is shaken with aqueous KI to give D. Identify C and D.
options: C = 1-bromo-4-methylbenzene; D cannot form because CuI is absent
questions.explanation:
A is p-toluidine (4-methylaniline). Diazotisation gives B, the 4-methylbenzenediazonium chloride.
Sandmeyer's reaction with CuBr replaces $-N_2^+$ by Br on the ring. So C is 1-bromo-4-methylbenzene; the methyl group is unaffected.
KI replaces $-N_2^+$ by I without any cuprous salt. So D is 1-iodo-4-methylbenzene, and option 4 is wrong.
Options 2 and 3 wrongly place the halogen on the side chain.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Grignard reagents are prepared and handled under strictly anhydrous conditions, using dry ether.
Reason (R): Grignard reagents react even with traces of water to form the corresponding hydrocarbons.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: RMgX is made by reacting a haloalkane with Mg in dry ether, and moisture must be excluded.
R is true: RMgX is highly reactive towards proton sources. For example, $RMgX + H_2O \rightarrow RH + Mg(OH)X$.
The reagent would be destroyed by any moisture, and this is exactly why dry conditions are needed. So R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements regarding nucleophilic substitution in haloarenes are correct?
(i) Chlorobenzene is converted to phenol by aqueous NaOH only at about 623 K and 300 atm.
(ii) In 4-nitrochlorobenzene, the negative charge of the carbanion formed after $OH^-$ attack is stabilised by the nitro group.
(iii) In 3-nitrochlorobenzene, one resonance structure of the carbanion places the negative charge on the carbon bearing –$NO_2$.
(iv) The phenyl cation is resonance stabilised, so haloarenes readily follow the SN1 path.
(v) The C–Cl bond in chlorobenzene has partial double bond character.
(vi) Repulsion between an electron-rich nucleophile and the electron-rich ring makes attack less likely.
(vii) A nitro group at the ortho position increases the reactivity of chlorobenzene.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct. These drastic conditions are given in NCERT.
(ii) Correct. The negative charge reaches the carbon bearing $NO_2$ and is delocalised onto the nitro group.
(iii) Incorrect. For a meta nitro group, no resonance structure puts the negative charge on that carbon.
(iv) Incorrect. The phenyl cation is not resonance stabilised, which rules out SN1.
(v) Correct. Resonance of the halogen lone pairs with the ring gives the C–Cl bond partial double bond character.
(vi) Correct. NCERT gives this repulsion as one of the reasons for low reactivity.
(vii) Correct. Ortho and para $NO_2$ groups activate the ring.
Correct statements = 5.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In the hydrolysis of tert-butyl bromide by hydroxide ion, doubling the concentration of $OH^-$ (keeping everything else the same) does not change the rate.
Statement II: In the slow step of this reaction, the C–Br bond breaks to form a carbocation, and the energy needed comes from solvation of the bromide ion by the polar protic solvent.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I: Correct. The reaction is $S_N1$ with Rate = $k[(CH_3)_3CBr]$. $OH^-$ is not involved in the slow step, so its concentration does not affect the rate.
Statement II: Correct. Step I is the slow, reversible heterolysis of C–Br, giving the tert-butyl carbocation. The energy for this bond breaking is obtained through solvation of $Br^-$ by the protons of the protic solvent.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chloroethane is treated with sodium ethoxide ($CH_3CH_2ONa$). What is the expected substitution product?
questions.explanation:
Sodium alkoxide $NaOR'$ supplies the nucleophile $R'O^-$.
This nucleophile displaces $Cl^-$ to give an ether, $ROR'$ (Table 6.4).
With R = R' = ethyl, the product is $CH_3CH_2OCH_2CH_3$, i.e. ethoxyethane.
Ethanol would need $OH^-$ or $H_2O$ as the nucleophile.
An ester needs a silver carboxylate.
Butane would come from a Wurtz reaction with Na metal.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Thionyl chloride is the preferred reagent for converting an alcohol into an alkyl chloride. What is the main reason?
options: It works only with tertiary alcohols, so no isomeric mixture forms
Both by-products, SO$_2$ and HCl, are gases that escape, leaving fairly pure alkyl chloride
It needs no heating and gives an alkyl chloride with retained optical rotation
Its by-product POCl$_3$ is easily removed by washing with water
questions.explanation:
R–OH + SOCl$_2$ → R–Cl + SO$_2$↑ + HCl↑
Both by-products are gases, so they leave the reaction mixture and the alkyl chloride is left nearly pure.
POCl$_3$ is a by-product of PCl$_5$, not of SOCl$_2$.
SOCl$_2$ is not restricted to tertiary alcohols.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the preparation of haloarenes is INCORRECT?
options: In Sandmeyer's reaction, the diazonium group is replaced by –Cl or –Br on mixing the diazonium salt solution with CuCl or CuBr
Replacement of the diazonium group by iodine needs CuI as a catalyst; KI alone does not react
The diazonium salt is obtained by treating a primary aromatic amine in cold aqueous mineral acid with sodium nitrite
Aryl chlorides and bromides can be made by electrophilic substitution using Fe or $FeCl_3$ as catalyst
questions.explanation:
Option 1 is correct: it describes Sandmeyer's reaction with cuprous halides.
Option 2 is incorrect: NCERT states that iodo substitution does not require a cuprous halide. Shaking the diazonium salt with KI is enough.
Option 3 is correct: this is how the diazonium salt is formed.
Option 4 is correct: electrophilic halogenation needs a Lewis acid catalyst.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Iodoform, once used as an antiseptic, has been replaced by other formulations containing iodine.
Reason (R): The antiseptic property of iodoform is due to the liberation of free iodine and not due to iodoform itself.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Iodoform has been replaced by other iodine-containing formulations.
R is true. Its antiseptic action comes from the free iodine it liberates.
However, NCERT gives a different reason for the replacement: iodoform's objectionable smell. R only explains how iodoform works as an antiseptic. Iodine-containing substitutes can supply iodine without the bad smell.
So R does not explain A.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: The dipole moment of chlorobenzene is lower than that of cyclohexyl chloride.
Statement II: The carbon bearing chlorine in chlorobenzene is $sp^2$ hybridised and is therefore less electronegative than the $sp^3$ carbon of cyclohexyl chloride, making the C–Cl bond in chlorobenzene more polar.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. In chlorobenzene, resonance gives the C–Cl bond partial double bond character, and the bond is shorter (169 pm vs 177 pm). Both lower the dipole moment.
Statement II is incorrect. An $sp^2$ carbon has greater s-character, so it is more electronegative, not less.
The $sp^2$ carbon holds the bonding pair more tightly. This reduces, rather than increases, the polarity of the C–Cl bond.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the common system of naming, the compound CH3CHCl2 is called:
questions.explanation:
In CH3CHCl2 both Cl atoms are on the same carbon, so it is a geminal (gem) dihalide.
In common names, gem-dihalides are called alkylidene halides. This makes CH3CHCl2 ethylidene chloride (IUPAC: 1,1-dichloroethane).
Ethylene dichloride is ClCH2CH2Cl, the vic-dihalide (alkylene dihalide).
Methylene chloride is CH2Cl2.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) William Nicol
(B) Louis Pasteur
(C) van't Hoff and Le Bel
(D) Polarimeter
List-II
(I) Proposed that the four groups around carbon are arranged tetrahedrally
(II) Measures the angle of rotation of plane polarised light
(III) Developed the first prism that produced plane polarised light
(IV) Observed mirror-image crystals whose solutions showed equal but opposite rotations
questions.explanation:
A-III: Nicol developed the first prism that produced plane polarised light.
B-IV: Pasteur (1848) observed mirror-image crystals whose solutions showed equal but opposite optical rotation.
C-I: van't Hoff and Le Bel (1874) independently proposed the tetrahedral arrangement of groups around carbon and introduced the idea of the asymmetric carbon.
D-II: A polarimeter measures the angle of rotation.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the stereochemistry of reactions at or near a chiral carbon.
(i) When (–)-2-methylbutan-1-ol is heated with concentrated HCl, the configuration at the stereocentre is retained because no bond to that carbon is broken.
(ii) A change in the sign of optical rotation from reactant to product always means that the configuration has been inverted.
(iii) Hydrolysis of (–)-2-bromooctane by NaOH via SN2 gives octan-2-ol with –OH on the side opposite to where Br was.
(iv) SN1 hydrolysis of optically active 2-bromobutane gives an optically inactive product because the planar $sp^2$ carbocation can be attacked from either face.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the C–OH bond being replaced is not on the stereocentre, so the configuration is retained, although the sign of rotation changes.
(ii) Incorrect: two different compounds with the same configuration can rotate light in opposite directions. The sign is not tied to configuration.
(iii) Correct: in SN2 the nucleophile attacks from the back side, giving inversion.
(iv) Correct: attack on the planar carbocation gives a racemic (±) mixture.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Chloroform is stored in closed, dark coloured bottles filled completely up to the brim.
Reason (R): In the presence of light, chloroform is slowly oxidised by air to carbonyl chloride (phosgene), an extremely poisonous gas.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT states that chloroform is kept in closed, dark bottles filled completely.
R is true: light and air together slowly oxidise CHCl$_3$ to COCl$_2$ (phosgene).
The dark glass cuts out light, and filling the bottle completely keeps out air. Both precautions block the oxidation, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Alkyl iodides are prepared by heating alcohols with KI in 95% orthophosphoric acid rather than in concentrated sulphuric acid.
Reason (R): Concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$ converts KI into HI and then oxidises HI to I$_2$.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: heating an alcohol with NaI or KI in 95% H$_3$PO$_4$ gives a good yield of R–I.
R is true: H$_2$SO$_4$ is an oxidising acid. It first forms HI from KI and then oxidises the HI to I$_2$, so no HI is left to react with the alcohol.
H$_3$PO$_4$ is non-oxidising, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: Paul Müller discovered the effectiveness of DDT as an insecticide and was awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine and Physiology in 1948.
Statement II: DDT was first synthesised in 1948, the same year in which its insecticidal property was recognised.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Paul Müller of Geigy Pharmaceuticals found that DDT was effective as an insecticide in 1939. He received the 1948 Nobel Prize in Medicine and Physiology for this discovery.
Statement II is incorrect. DDT was first prepared in 1873. Its insecticidal action was discovered in 1939, not 1948.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Although chlorine deactivates the benzene ring, chlorobenzene undergoes electrophilic substitution mainly at the ortho and para positions.
Reason (R): The inductive effect of chlorine controls the orientation of substitution, whereas its resonance effect controls the reactivity of the ring.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Chlorine is slightly deactivating, yet it is o,p-directing.
R is false because the roles are reversed.
The –I effect is the stronger effect, so it causes net deactivation and controls reactivity.
The +R effect raises electron density mainly at the ortho and para positions. It also stabilises the carbocation formed by attack at those positions, so it controls orientation.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For a given alkyl group R, which of the following correctly shows the order of boiling points of the alkyl halides?
questions.explanation:
Moving from F to I, the halogen atom becomes larger and heavier and carries more electrons.
This strengthens the van der Waals forces between the molecules, so more energy is needed to boil the liquid.
The boiling point therefore rises steadily from RF to RI, giving RI > RBr > RCl > RF.
Option (1) is the reverse of this order. It might be chosen by someone who links boiling point to the electronegativity of fluorine.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A chemist heats tetrachloromethane with $SbF_3$ to obtain Freon 12. Which option correctly identifies the product, the type of reaction, and the reason this freon harms the ozone layer?
options: $CCl_3F$; Finkelstein halogen exchange; it is toxic and reacts with ozone in the lower atmosphere
$CCl_2F_2$; Swarts halogen exchange; being extremely stable, it diffuses unchanged into the stratosphere and initiates radical chain reactions there
$CCl_2F_2$; Swarts halogen exchange; it is corrosive and readily decomposes in the troposphere, releasing chlorine
$CF_4$; free radical fluorination; it absorbs ultraviolet rays near the ground
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Freon 12 is $CCl_2F_2$. Here two Cl atoms of $CCl_4$ are replaced by F.
Step 2: Heating an alkyl chloride with a metallic fluoride such as $SbF_3$ is the Swarts reaction. Finkelstein uses NaI and gives iodides.
Step 3: Freons are extremely stable, unreactive, non-toxic and non-corrosive. Because they do not break down low in the atmosphere, they diffuse unchanged into the stratosphere. There they start radical chains that upset the ozone balance.
Option (3) fails because freons are non-corrosive and do not readily decompose in the troposphere.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An alkene X ($C_5H_{10}$) reacts with HBr to give a tertiary bromide as the major product. With $Br_2$ in $CCl_4$, X gives 2,3-dibromo-2-methylbutane. X is:
questions.explanation:
Br$_2$ adds to the two carbons of the C=C bond. In the product the Br atoms sit on C-2 and C-3, so the double bond in X lies between C-2 and C-3 of a 2-methylbutane skeleton. That is $(CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3$, 2-methylbut-2-ene.
Check with HBr: by Markovnikov's rule, H adds to C-3 and Br to C-2, giving the tertiary bromide $(CH_3)_2CBrCH_2CH_3$.
2-Methylbut-1-ene also gives this tertiary bromide, but with Br$_2$ it forms 1,2-dibromo-2-methylbutane, so it fails the second test.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorobenzene can be converted into phenol only under drastic conditions. Which set of conditions is used for this conversion?
options: Heating with aqueous NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm, followed by acidification
Shaking with aqueous NaOH at room temperature and 1 atm
Heating with alcoholic KOH under reflux at 1 atm
Warming with dilute NaOH at 373 K and 1 atm
questions.explanation:
Chlorobenzene is very unreactive towards nucleophilic substitution because its C–Cl bond has partial double bond character.
So hydrolysis needs aqueous NaOH at about 623 K and 300 atm. This gives sodium phenoxide, which on acidification gives phenol.
Room-temperature or 373 K conditions are far too mild for an unactivated haloarene.
Alcoholic KOH is used for dehydrohalogenation of haloalkanes, not for making phenol.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The IUPAC name of o-chlorotoluene is 1-chloro-2-methylbenzene.
Reason (R): For disubstituted benzenes, the prefixes o-, m- and p- of the common system are replaced by the locants 1,2; 1,3 and 1,4 in the IUPAC system.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. In o-chlorotoluene, Cl and CH3 are on adjacent ring carbons. Its IUPAC name is 1-chloro-2-methylbenzene, also written 2-chlorotoluene (Table 6.1).
R is true. NCERT states that IUPAC uses the numerals 1,2; 1,3 and 1,4 in place of o-, m-, p-.
The ortho relationship becomes the locants 1,2, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (halogen-containing compound) with List-II (use or significance):
List-I
(A) Chloramphenicol
(B) Thyroxine
(C) Chloroquine
(D) Halothane
List-II
(I) Treatment of malaria
(II) Anaesthetic used during surgery
(III) Antibiotic effective against typhoid fever
(IV) Iodine-containing hormone; its deficiency causes goiter
questions.explanation:
(A) Chloramphenicol is a chlorine-containing antibiotic made by microorganisms. It is used to treat typhoid, so A matches III.
(B) Thyroxine is an iodine-containing hormone made by the body. Its deficiency causes goiter, so B matches IV.
(C) Chloroquine is a synthetic halogen compound used for malaria, so C matches I.
(D) Halothane is used as an anaesthetic during surgery, so D matches II.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) The C–Cl bond in chlorobenzene (169 pm) is shorter than that in a chloroalkane (177 pm).
(ii) Chlorobenzene is hydrolysed by an SN1 path because the phenyl cation is stabilised by resonance.
(iii) A $-NO_2$ group para to chlorine stabilises the carbanion formed when a nucleophile attacks the ring.
(iv) 1-Chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene needs harsher conditions for hydrolysis than chlorobenzene.
(v) Repulsion between an electron-rich nucleophile and the electron-rich arene ring makes nucleophilic attack on haloarenes less likely.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the $sp^2$ carbon and resonance shorten the bond to 169 pm, versus 177 pm in a chloroalkane.
(ii) Incorrect: the phenyl cation is NOT resonance stabilised, so the SN1 path is ruled out.
(iii) Correct: the negative charge delocalises onto the o/p-positioned $-NO_2$ group.
(iv) Incorrect: more o/p nitro groups make the reaction easier, so milder conditions are needed.
(v) Correct: this is one of the reasons NCERT lists.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In electrophilic substitution of chlorobenzene, the –I effect of chlorine controls the overall reactivity, while its +R effect controls the orientation of the incoming group.
Statement II: Electrophilic substitution in chlorobenzene takes place faster and under milder conditions than in benzene.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
Statement I is true. The –I effect of Cl is stronger than its +R effect, so there is a net withdrawal of electrons and the ring is deactivated. Resonance increases the electron density at the o/p positions, so it decides where the electrophile attacks.
Statement II is false. Because the ring is deactivated, substitution in chlorobenzene is slower and needs more drastic conditions than in benzene.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the bonding in a Grignard reagent, RMgX, is correct?
options: Both the C–Mg and Mg–X bonds are essentially ionic
The C–Mg bond is covalent but highly polar, while the Mg–X bond is essentially ionic
The C–Mg bond is non-polar covalent, while the Mg–X bond is polar covalent
The C–Mg bond is polar with carbon carrying a partial positive charge
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that the C–Mg bond in RMgX is covalent but highly polar.
Carbon pulls electrons from the electropositive Mg, so carbon carries a partial negative charge. This rules out option 4.
The Mg–X bond is essentially ionic.
Option 1 is wrong because the C–Mg bond is not ionic. Option 3 is wrong because the C–Mg bond is not non-polar.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (bond in $CH_3X$) with List-II (property value) using periodic trends.
List-I:
(A) C–F
(B) C–Cl
(C) C–Br
(D) C–I
List-II:
(i) Dipole moment 1.636 D
(ii) Bond enthalpy 452 kJ/mol
(iii) Bond length 193 pm
(iv) Dipole moment 1.860 D
questions.explanation:
A: C–F is the shortest and strongest bond, so it has the highest bond enthalpy, 452 kJ/mol, giving (ii).
B: $CH_3Cl$ has the highest dipole moment among the methyl halides, 1.860 D, giving (iv).
C: bond length grows from 178 pm (C–Cl) to 214 pm (C–I), so 193 pm fits C–Br, giving (iii).
D: $CH_3I$ has the lowest dipole moment, 1.636 D, giving (i).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (name reaction) with List-II (description):
List-I
(a) Finkelstein reaction
(b) Swarts reaction
(c) Wurtz-Fittig reaction
(d) Sandmeyer reaction
List-II
(i) Alkyl halide and aryl halide treated together with sodium in dry ether
(ii) Alkyl chloride heated with NaI in dry acetone
(iii) Freshly prepared benzenediazonium salt mixed with CuCl
(iv) Alkyl bromide heated with AgF
questions.explanation:
(a)-(ii): Finkelstein reaction is halogen exchange with NaI in dry acetone. NaCl precipitates, which drives the reaction forward.
(b)-(iv): Swarts reaction converts an alkyl chloride or bromide into an alkyl fluoride using a metallic fluoride such as AgF, $Hg_2F_2$, $CoF_2$ or $SbF_3$.
(c)-(i): Wurtz-Fittig reaction couples an alkyl halide and an aryl halide with Na in dry ether to give an alkylarene.
(d)-(iii): Sandmeyer reaction replaces the diazonium group with –Cl using CuCl.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about preparing halo compounds from hydroxy compounds is INCORRECT?
options: Tertiary alcohols give alkyl chlorides simply on shaking with concentrated HCl at room temperature
Primary and secondary alcohols need ZnCl$_2$ as a catalyst for their reaction with HCl
Phenol is readily converted into chlorobenzene by heating with HCl in the presence of ZnCl$_2$
Constant boiling HBr (48%) is used to prepare alkyl bromides from alcohols
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: tertiary alcohols are the most reactive (order 3° > 2° > 1°), so shaking with conc. HCl is enough.
(2) Correct: ZnCl$_2$ is required for 1° and 2° alcohols.
(3) Incorrect: in phenol the C–O bond has partial double bond character. It is stronger than a single bond and hard to break, so these methods do not give aryl halides.
(4) Correct: constant boiling 48% HBr is used for alkyl bromides.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reagent used on an alcohol) with List-II (feature).
List-I
(A) $SOCl_2$
(B) Conc. HCl + anhydrous $ZnCl_2$
(C) Red phosphorus + $I_2$
(D) NaI/KI in 95% $H_3PO_4$
List-II
(i) Catalyst needed when the alcohol is primary or secondary
(ii) Heating gives good yields of alkyl iodide
(iii) Gaseous by-products give a pure alkyl chloride
(iv) Generates the phosphorus halide in situ
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A: $SOCl_2$ forms gaseous $SO_2$ and HCl, so the product is pure, giving (iii).
B: $ZnCl_2$ is required with HCl for 1° and 2° alcohols, giving (i).
C: Red P and $I_2$ produce $PI_3$ in the reaction mixture, giving (iv).
D: Heating with NaI/KI in 95% $H_3PO_4$ gives good yields of R–I, giving (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following molecules are chiral?
2-Chlorobutane, propan-2-ol, bromochloroiodomethane (BrClCHI), 2-bromopropanoic acid, 1-chlorobutane, 2,3-dihydroxypropanal, 3-chloropentane
questions.explanation:
A molecule with one carbon bearing four different groups is chiral.
Chiral: 2-chlorobutane (H, Cl, CH3, C2H5); BrClCHI; 2-bromopropanoic acid (H, Br, CH3, COOH); 2,3-dihydroxypropanal (H, OH, CHO, CH2OH).
Achiral: propan-2-ol (two CH3 groups); 1-chlorobutane (no stereocentre); 3-chloropentane (two C2H5 groups on the C–Cl carbon).
The total is 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Thionyl chloride is often preferred over $PCl_5$ or HCl for converting an alcohol into an alkyl chloride. What is the main reason?
options: Thionyl chloride converts tertiary alcohols but not primary alcohols
The by-products $SO_2$ and HCl are gases that escape, leaving a pure alkyl chloride
Thionyl chloride needs anhydrous $ZnCl_2$ as a catalyst, which increases the yield
The by-product of the reaction is $POCl_3$, which is easy to distil off
questions.explanation:
Reaction: $ROH + SOCl_2 \rightarrow RCl + SO_2\uparrow + HCl\uparrow$.
Both by-products are gases, so they leave the reaction mixture and the alkyl chloride is obtained pure.
$POCl_3$ is a by-product of the $PCl_5$ reaction, not the $SOCl_2$ reaction. $ZnCl_2$ is the catalyst used with HCl.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the following sequence:
1-Bromo-2-methylpropane $\xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH, heat}}$ P $\xrightarrow{\text{HBr}}$ Q $\xrightarrow{\text{Mg, dry ether}}$ R $\xrightarrow{H_2O}$ S
What is the final product S?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: $\beta$-elimination of $(CH_3)_2CHCH_2Br$ gives P, $(CH_3)_2C=CH_2$ (2-methylpropene).
Step 2: HBr adds to P by Markovnikov's rule, giving Q, $(CH_3)_3CBr$.
Step 3: Q reacts with Mg in dry ether to form the Grignard reagent R, $(CH_3)_3CMgBr$.
Step 4: Water protonates R to give the hydrocarbon S, $(CH_3)_3CH$, which is 2-methylpropane.
Why the alcohol is wrong: water acts as a proton source for RMgX, so it gives an alkane, not an alcohol.
Why 2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane is wrong: that coupling product would need a Wurtz reaction.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chloroform is stored in closed, dark-coloured bottles that are filled completely to the top. What is the main reason for this practice?
options: To prevent its slow oxidation by air in the presence of light to poisonous phosgene
To prevent it from absorbing moisture and changing into iodoform
To stop it from polymerising into a solid in sunlight
To prevent it from losing its sweet smell by evaporation
questions.explanation:
In the presence of light, air slowly oxidises chloroform to carbonyl chloride ($COCl_2$), also called phosgene. Phosgene is an extremely poisonous gas.
Dark bottles cut off the light. Filling the bottle completely leaves no room for air.
Together, these remove both conditions needed for the oxidation.
Chloroform does not change into iodoform or polymerise, so options (2) and (3) are wrong. Option (4) ignores the real hazard, which is phosgene formation.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider all eight structural isomers of molecular formula $C_5H_{11}Br$. Which pair correctly gives the number of primary (1°) bromides among them and the number of these isomers that are chiral?
questions.explanation:
Primary isomers: 1-bromopentane, 1-bromo-3-methylbutane, 1-bromo-2-methylbutane and 1-bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane. That makes 4.
Secondary isomers: 2-bromopentane, 3-bromopentane and 2-bromo-3-methylbutane. That makes 3.
Tertiary isomer: 2-bromo-2-methylbutane. That makes 1.
A chiral isomer needs a carbon carrying four different groups:
- 2-bromopentane: C-2 has H, Br, $CH_3$, $C_3H_7$.
- 2-bromo-3-methylbutane: C-2 has H, Br, $CH_3$, $CH(CH_3)_2$.
- 1-bromo-2-methylbutane: C-2 has H, $CH_3$, $C_2H_5$, $CH_2Br$.
So 3 isomers are chiral. 3-Bromopentane is achiral because its C-3 carries two ethyl groups.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Fluorobenzene is not prepared by directly treating benzene with fluorine in the presence of a Lewis acid. Why?
options: Fluorine is too unreactive to attack the benzene ring
Fluorine is so highly reactive that the reaction cannot be controlled
The reaction is reversible, and the HF formed must be oxidised
Fluorine cannot be polarised by any Lewis acid
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that fluoro compounds are not made by electrophilic substitution because fluorine is highly reactive.
The reaction is violent and cannot be controlled to give a single monofluoro product.
Option 1 reverses the actual fact.
Option 3 describes iodination, which is the reversible reaction that needs an oxidising agent.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A nitro group at the meta position of chlorobenzene markedly increases its reactivity towards nucleophilic substitution by $OH^-$.
Reason (R): The nitro group is an electron-withdrawing group.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
R is true. –$NO_2$ withdraws electron density from the benzene ring.
A is false. A nitro group activates the ring only at the ortho and para positions, where it can stabilise the negative charge of the carbanion intermediate through resonance.
At the meta position, no resonance structure places the negative charge on the carbon bearing –$NO_2$. NCERT therefore states that a meta nitro group has no effect on reactivity.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: Ethylmagnesium bromide reacts with water to form ethane.
Statement II: Grignard reagents are prepared in dry ether because even traces of moisture convert them into hydrocarbons.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. $C_2H_5MgBr + H_2O \rightarrow C_2H_6 + Mg(OH)Br$, because the polar C–Mg bond lets the ethyl group take up a proton from water.
Statement II is correct. Grignard reagents react with any source of protons, so moisture must be excluded. That is why they are made in dry ether.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 1-Chloropropane is treated separately with (a) aqueous KOH and (b) alcoholic KOH. The major products of (a) and (b), respectively, are:
questions.explanation:
In aqueous KOH, $OH^-$ acts mainly as a nucleophile. Substitution gives the alcohol, propan-1-ol.
In alcoholic KOH, the base removes a β-hydrogen. Together with loss of $Cl^-$ from the α-carbon, this β-elimination gives the alkene, propene.
Option 1 reverses the two conditions.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: Benzyl chloride contains a C–Cl bond in which the carbon is $sp^3$ hybridised, even though the molecule has an aromatic ring.
Statement II: In allylic halides, the halogen is bonded to an $sp^2$-hybridised carbon of the C=C double bond.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. In C6H5CH2Cl the Cl is on the CH2 carbon, which is $sp^3$ and only attached to the ring. Benzylic halides therefore belong to the $sp^3$ C–X class.
Statement II is incorrect. In allylic halides the halogen is on an $sp^3$ carbon adjacent to the C=C.
A halogen on an $sp^2$ carbon of the C=C defines a vinylic halide instead.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: When toluene is chlorinated in the presence of $FeCl_3$, the ortho and para isomers formed can be separated easily.
Statement II: p-Chlorotoluene has a much higher melting point than o-chlorotoluene because the symmetrical para isomer packs better in the crystal lattice.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT states that the o- and p-isomers obtained from electrophilic halogenation are easily separated.
Statement II is correct. The separation works because of the large difference in their melting points. The para isomer melts higher due to its symmetry and better fit in the lattice, so it can be crystallised out.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider free radical monochlorination of 2-methylbutane, $(CH_3)_2CHCH_2CH_3$.
Statement I: Four structural isomers of $C_5H_{11}Cl$ are possible, and exactly two of them contain an asymmetric carbon atom.
Statement II: Among these products, 2-chloro-2-methylbutane undergoes SN1 hydrolysis faster than 1-chloro-3-methylbutane.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
2-Methylbutane has four types of H, so it gives four structural isomers.
1-Chloro-2-methylbutane: C2 carries H, $CH_3$, $CH_2Cl$ and $C_2H_5$, so it is chiral.
2-Chloro-3-methylbutane: C2 carries H, Cl, $CH_3$ and isopropyl, so it is chiral.
2-Chloro-2-methylbutane and 1-chloro-3-methylbutane have no stereocentre. Exactly two products are chiral, so Statement I is correct.
Statement II is correct. The tertiary chloride forms a stable 3° carbocation, while the primary chloride would have to form an unstable 1° carbocation.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): 1-Chloro-3-nitrobenzene (m-nitrochlorobenzene) is not appreciably more reactive than chlorobenzene towards replacement of Cl by OH⁻, whereas the ortho- and para-isomers react much more readily.
Reason (R): In the carbanion formed by attack of OH⁻ on the meta-isomer, none of the resonance structures places the negative charge on the carbon carrying the –NO2 group, so –NO2 cannot stabilise it.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
When OH⁻ adds to the carbon bearing Cl, the negative charge spreads to the ortho- and para-positions relative to Cl.
In the o- and p-nitro isomers, one resonance form puts the charge on the carbon bearing –NO2. The nitro group delocalises it, stabilising the carbanion and speeding up the reaction.
In the m-isomer, this charge never reaches the carbon bearing –NO2, so there is no stabilisation and no rate effect.
A is true, and R is true and explains it.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reagent used on an alcohol) with List-II (feature of the reaction).
List-I
(a) SOCl$_2$
(b) PCl$_5$
(c) PCl$_3$
(d) Red P + Br$_2$
List-II
(i) H$_3$PO$_3$ is formed as a by-product
(ii) Phosphorus trihalide is generated in situ
(iii) Both by-products are gases
(iv) POCl$_3$ and HCl are by-products
questions.explanation:
(a) SOCl$_2$ gives R–Cl + SO$_2$ + HCl; both by-products are gases → (iii).
(b) R–OH + PCl$_5$ → R–Cl + POCl$_3$ + HCl → (iv).
(c) 3R–OH + PCl$_3$ → 3R–Cl + H$_3$PO$_3$ → (i).
(d) Red P reacts with Br$_2$ to form PBr$_3$ in the reaction mixture (in situ) → (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reaction of chlorobenzene) with List-II (main organic product):
List-I
(a) $CH_3Cl$, anhydrous $AlCl_3$
(b) Na, dry ether
(c) $CH_3Cl$ and Na, dry ether
(d) Conc. $H_2SO_4$, heat
List-II
(i) Biphenyl
(ii) 2-Chlorotoluene and 4-chlorotoluene
(iii) Toluene
(iv) 2- and 4-Chlorobenzenesulphonic acid
questions.explanation:
(a) This is Friedel–Crafts alkylation. Ring H is replaced at the o/p positions while Cl stays, giving 2- and 4-chlorotoluene → (ii).
(b) This is the Fittig reaction. Two phenyl groups couple to give biphenyl → (i).
(c) This is the Wurtz–Fittig reaction. The aryl and alkyl groups join to give toluene → (iii).
(d) This is sulphonation at the o/p positions, giving chlorobenzenesulphonic acids → (iv).
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
(–)-2-Methylbutan-1-ol is heated with concentrated HCl to give (+)-1-chloro-2-methylbutane.
Statement I: The configuration at the asymmetric carbon is retained, because no bond to the stereocentre is broken in this reaction.
Statement II: Whenever configuration is retained in a reaction, the sign of optical rotation of the product must be the same as that of the reactant.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The –OH is on C-1, which is not the stereocentre. The bonds at C-2 remain intact, so the configuration is retained.
Statement II is incorrect. Here the configuration is retained, yet the sign changes from (–) to (+).
Two different compounds with the same configuration can rotate light in opposite directions.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider all eight structural isomers having the molecular formula C5H11Br. How many of them contain an asymmetric (chiral) carbon atom?
questions.explanation:
Check each isomer for a carbon bearing four different groups:
1-Bromopentane, 1-bromo-3-methylbutane and 1-bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane have no stereocentre.
3-Bromopentane: no, because C-3 carries two identical ethyl groups. 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane: no, because C-2 carries two methyl groups.
2-Bromopentane: yes, C-2 has H, Br, CH3 and C3H7. 2-Bromo-3-methylbutane: yes, C-2 has H, Br, CH3 and CH(CH3)2.
1-Bromo-2-methylbutane: yes, C-2 has H, CH3, C2H5 and CH2Br.
Total = 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: p-Dichlorobenzene has a higher melting point than o-dichlorobenzene and m-dichlorobenzene.
Statement II: p-Dichlorobenzene has a much higher boiling point than its ortho and meta isomers.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The para isomer is symmetrical, so it fits better into the crystal lattice and melts at a higher temperature.
Statement II is incorrect. NCERT notes that the boiling points of isomeric dihalobenzenes are very nearly the same. Symmetry affects packing in the solid, which changes the melting point, not the boiling point.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Arrange the following bromides in decreasing order of reactivity towards $S_N2$ displacement by $OH^-$:
(P) $CH_3Br$
(Q) $(CH_3)_3CCH_2Br$
(R) $CH_3CH_2CH_2Br$
(S) $(CH_3)_2CHCH_2Br$
questions.explanation:
$S_N2$ rate is controlled by crowding around the carbon bearing Br.
P ($CH_3Br$) carries only three small H atoms, so it is fastest.
R, S and Q are all primary bromides, but they differ in branching at the adjacent (β) carbon.
R has no β-branching. S has one β-methyl. Q (neopentyl bromide) has a bulky tert-butyl group next to the reacting carbon, which strongly hinders backside attack.
The order is therefore P > R > S > Q.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A compound rotates the plane of plane polarised light in the clockwise direction. Which description of this compound is correct?
options: Laevorotatory, l-form, (–) sign before the rotation
Dextrorotatory, d-form, (+) sign before the rotation
Dextrorotatory, l-form, (+) sign before the rotation
Laevorotatory, d-form, (–) sign before the rotation
questions.explanation:
Clockwise rotation means rotation to the right.
Such a compound is called dextrorotatory, or the d-form.
Its rotation is written with a positive (+) sign.
Anticlockwise rotation would make it laevorotatory (l-form) with a (–) sign.
Options (3) and (4) mix the terms of the two forms, so they are wrong.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In a haloalkane such as $CH_3Cl$, how is the electron density distributed in the carbon–halogen bond?
options: Carbon carries a partial positive charge ($\delta+$) and chlorine carries a partial negative charge ($\delta-$)
Carbon carries a partial negative charge ($\delta-$) and chlorine carries a partial positive charge ($\delta+$)
The bond is non-polar because carbon and chlorine share the electrons equally
Both carbon and chlorine carry partial positive charges
questions.explanation:
Halogens are more electronegative than carbon.
So the shared electron pair of the C–X bond is pulled towards the halogen.
The halogen therefore carries $\delta-$ and carbon carries $\delta+$. This makes carbon the electron-deficient site that nucleophiles attack.
Option (2) reverses the polarity, and the bond is clearly not non-polar.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When bromine in CCl$_4$ is added dropwise to cyclohexene, the reddish-brown colour disappears. What type of product is formed?
options: A gem-dibromide, which is reddish brown
A monobromo substitution product along with HBr
questions.explanation:
Br$_2$ adds across the C=C bond, so the two Br atoms end up on adjacent carbons. This gives a vicinal (vic) dibromide, here 1,2-dibromocyclohexane.
The vic-dibromide is colourless, so the bromine colour is discharged.
This decolourisation is the laboratory test for unsaturation.
Addition does not put both Br atoms on the same carbon, so no gem-dibromide forms.
No substitution occurs, so no HBr is released.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following molecules are chiral?
2-Chlorobutane, propan-2-ol, bromochloroiodomethane, 2-bromopropanoic acid, 1-chlorobutane, 3-chloropentane
questions.explanation:
A molecule here is chiral if it has a carbon bearing four different groups.
2-Chlorobutane: C2 carries H, Cl, $CH_3$ and $C_2H_5$, so it is chiral.
Propan-2-ol: C2 carries two $CH_3$ groups, so it is achiral.
BrClCHI: four different atoms on one carbon, so it is chiral.
2-Bromopropanoic acid: C2 carries H, Br, $CH_3$ and COOH, so it is chiral.
1-Chlorobutane has no stereocentre, and 3-chloropentane has two identical ethyl groups on C3, so both are achiral.
Total chiral molecules = 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Grignard reagents, RMgX, is INCORRECT?
options: They are obtained by reacting haloalkanes with magnesium metal in dry ether.
In RMgX, the C–Mg bond is essentially ionic, while the Mg–X bond is covalent and only weakly polar.
Amines are acidic enough to convert RMgX into the hydrocarbon RH.
Reacting RMgX with water is one way of converting an alkyl halide into a hydrocarbon.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: RX + Mg in dry ether gives RMgX.
(2) Incorrect: the bonding is the reverse of what is stated. According to NCERT, the C–Mg bond is covalent but highly polar, with carbon pulling electrons from the electropositive Mg. The Mg–X bond is essentially ionic.
(3) Correct: water, alcohols and amines all supply protons to RMgX and give RH.
(4) Correct: NCERT notes that this hydrolysis is a method for converting halides into hydrocarbons.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: Chlorobenzene undergoes electrophilic substitution more slowly than benzene and needs more drastic conditions.
Statement II: In chlorobenzene, the orientation of the incoming electrophile is controlled mainly by the –I effect of chlorine, which directs it to ortho- and para-positions.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The stronger –I effect of Cl withdraws electron density from the ring, so the ring is deactivated relative to benzene.
Statement II is incorrect. Orientation is controlled by the resonance (+R) effect, which raises electron density at the ortho- and para-positions. The inductive effect controls reactivity, not orientation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the $S_N1$ reaction of alkyl halides is correct?
options: Its rate depends on the concentrations of both the alkyl halide and the hydroxide ion.
It proceeds best in non-polar solvents, because solvation of the halide ion slows down C–X bond cleavage.
Benzyl bromide reacts faster than 1-bromopropane because the benzylic carbocation is stabilised by resonance.
Hydrolysis of optically active 2-bromobutane gives a single product with an inverted configuration.
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: The slow step is ionisation of R–X, so the rate depends only on [RX]. The reaction is first order.
(2) Incorrect: $S_N1$ reactions are favoured in polar protic solvents. Solvation of the halide ion supplies the energy needed to break the C–X bond.
(3) Correct: The benzylic cation is resonance stabilised, while the primary propyl cation is not. Benzyl bromide therefore ionises much faster.
(4) Incorrect: The carbocation intermediate is planar ($sp^2$) and can be attacked from either face. This gives racemisation, giving (±)-butan-2-ol. Inversion is characteristic of $S_N2$.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The dipole moment of $CH_3Cl$ is greater than that of $CH_3F$.
Reason (R): Fluorine is more electronegative than chlorine.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: $CH_3Cl$ has 1.860 D and $CH_3F$ has 1.847 D.
R is true: F is the most electronegative halogen.
However, R alone would predict a larger dipole moment for $CH_3F$, which is the opposite of A.
A is actually explained by the much longer C–Cl bond (178 pm vs 139 pm). Dipole moment = charge × distance, so the longer bond outweighs the smaller charge separation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The C–I bond enthalpy in $CH_3I$ is 234 kJ/mol. How much energy is required to break the C–I bonds in all the molecules present in 28.4 g of $CH_3I$? (Molar mass of $CH_3I$ = 142 g/mol)
questions.explanation:
Given: mass = 28.4 g, M = 142 g/mol, C–I bond enthalpy = 234 kJ/mol.
Formula: energy = moles × bond enthalpy, with one C–I bond per molecule.
Substituting: moles = 28.4/142 = 0.2 mol, so energy = 0.2 × 234 kJ.
So energy = 46.8 kJ.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Chlorides, bromides and iodides boil considerably higher than hydrocarbons of comparable molecular mass.
(ii) 1-Iodopropane is denser than 1-bromopropane.
(iii) Density decreases in the order CH2Cl2 > CHCl3 > CCl4.
(iv) The boiling points of o-, m- and p-dichlorobenzene differ widely.
(v) Haloalkanes dissolve in organic solvents because the new attractions formed are of nearly the same strength as those broken.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct. Halogen compounds are more polar and heavier, so their dipole-dipole and van der Waals forces are stronger.
(ii) Correct. Iodine has a higher atomic mass, so density is 1.747 vs 1.335 g/mL.
(iii) Incorrect. Density increases with more Cl atoms: 1.336 < 1.489 < 1.595 g/mL.
(iv) Incorrect. Their boiling points are very nearly the same.
(v) Correct, as stated in NCERT.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Thionyl chloride is preferred over phosphorus halides for converting an alcohol into a pure alkyl chloride.
Reason (R): In the reaction with thionyl chloride, the by-products $SO_2$ and HCl are gases that escape from the reaction mixture.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that thionyl chloride is the preferred reagent for making alkyl chlorides from alcohols.
R is true. $ROH + SOCl_2 \rightarrow RCl + SO_2 + HCl$, and both by-products are gases.
R explains A. The gaseous by-products leave the mixture, so only the alkyl chloride remains and no separation is needed.
Answer: (1)
