questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following give the stated haloarene as the main product in reasonable yield?
(i) Benzene + $Br_2$ / $FeBr_3$ → bromobenzene
(ii) Benzenediazonium chloride + KI (shaken) → iodobenzene
(iii) Phenol + conc. HCl / $ZnCl_2$ → chlorobenzene
(iv) Benzene + $F_2$ / $FeF_3$ → fluorobenzene
(v) Benzenediazonium chloride + CuCl → chlorobenzene
(vi) Benzene + $I_2$ alone (no oxidising agent) → iodobenzene
questions.explanation:
(i) Works: this is electrophilic bromination with a Lewis acid.
(ii) Works: KI replaces the diazonium group without any cuprous salt.
(iii) Fails: the C–O bond of phenol has partial double bond character and does not break.
(iv) Fails: fluorine is too reactive for controlled substitution.
(v) Works: this is Sandmeyer's reaction.
(vi) Fails: iodination is reversible without an oxidant to remove HI.
Three conversions work.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): When an animal ingests DDT at a steady rate, the amount of DDT in its body keeps building up over time.
Reason (R): DDT is chemically stable and fat soluble, and it is not metabolised rapidly by animals, so it gets stored in fatty tissues.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT notes that with continued ingestion, DDT builds up within the animal over time.
R is true. DDT is chemically stable and fat soluble, and animals do not metabolise it rapidly.
Because the body cannot break DDT down, it is deposited in fatty tissues instead of being removed. This is exactly why it accumulates, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) An $S_N2$ reaction occurs in a single step without any intermediate.
(ii) In the $S_N2$ transition state, the attacked carbon is simultaneously bonded to five atoms.
(iii) The carbocation formed in an $S_N1$ reaction is $sp^2$ hybridised and planar.
(iv) $S_N1$ reaction of an optically active alkyl halide gives a product with complete inversion of configuration.
(v) The rate of an $S_N2$ reaction is independent of the concentration of the nucleophile.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: bond making and bond breaking occur together in one step.
(ii) Correct: the nucleophile and the leaving group are both partially bonded to carbon, along with three other groups.
(iii) Correct: the carbocation is $sp^2$ and planar, so it is achiral.
(iv) Incorrect: attack can occur from both faces of the planar carbocation, so $S_N1$ gives racemisation. Inversion is the hallmark of $S_N2$.
(v) Incorrect: $S_N2$ is second order, rate = k[RX][Nu].
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about dichloromethane (methylene chloride) is INCORRECT?
options: It is used as a paint remover and as a propellant in aerosols.
Exposure to lower levels of it in air can lead to slightly impaired hearing and vision.
Direct contact with the eyes can burn the cornea.
Its major use today is in the production of the freon refrigerant R-22.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct. Dichloromethane is used as a paint remover, an aerosol propellant, a process solvent for drugs and a metal-cleaning solvent.
(2) Correct. Low-level exposure slightly impairs hearing and vision, because it harms the central nervous system.
(3) Correct. Direct contact with the eyes can burn the cornea.
(4) Incorrect. Making the refrigerant R-22 is the major present-day use of chloroform ($CHCl_3$), not dichloromethane.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following haloalkanes is a gas at room temperature?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: methyl chloride, methyl bromide, ethyl chloride and some chlorofluoromethanes are gases at room temperature. Higher members are liquids or solids.
Ethyl chloride fits this list, so it is a gas.
Chloroform and carbon tetrachloride are polychloro compounds. Their larger molecular mass and stronger intermolecular forces make them liquids.
1-Iodopropane is a liquid because of the heavy, highly polarisable iodine atom.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Using the NCERT density data for haloalkanes, which one of the following liquids is lighter than water (density 1.0 g/mL)?
questions.explanation:
NCERT: bromo, iodo and polychloro derivatives are heavier than water.
Density rises with the atomic mass of the halogen and with the number of halogen atoms.
n-C$_3$H$_7$Cl has only one Cl, which is a light halogen, so its density is 0.89 g/mL. This is less than water.
n-C$_3$H$_7$Br (1.335), CHCl$_3$ (1.489) and CCl$_4$ (1.595) all have densities above 1 g/mL.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Each of the following liquids is shaken with water and allowed to settle. Which one will form the upper layer, floating on water (density of water = 1.0 g/mL)?
questions.explanation:
A liquid floats on water only if its density is less than 1.0 g/mL. Table 6.3 gives the values:
n-C3H7Cl = 0.89 g/mL, which is less than water, so it floats.
n-C3H7Br = 1.335, CH2Cl2 = 1.336 and CHCl3 = 1.489 g/mL are all denser than water, so they sink.
This matches the NCERT statement that bromo, iodo and polychloro derivatives are heavier than water.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Optically pure (–)-2-bromobutane is hydrolysed under conditions where part of it reacts by SN2 and the rest by SN1 (assume no elimination).
- The SN2 path gives only (+)-butan-2-ol.
- The SN1 path gives a 50:50 mixture of the two enantiomers.
A solution of pure (+)-butan-2-ol shows a rotation of $+13.5^\circ$. The product alcohol, at the same total concentration and under identical conditions, shows a rotation of $+5.4^\circ$. What percentage of the bromide reacted by the SN2 path?
questions.explanation:
Given: pure (+)-alcohol gives $+13.5^\circ$; the product mixture gives $+5.4^\circ$.
Idea: the racemic portion from SN1 has zero net rotation, because the rotations of the two enantiomers cancel. Only the excess (+)-alcohol from SN2 contributes.
Fraction via SN2 = 5.4 / 13.5 = 0.40.
So 40% reacted by SN2 and 60% by SN1. The 60% option is the tempting wrong choice, since it is the SN1 share.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Iodination of benzene with $I_2$ is carried out in the presence of $HNO_3$ or $HIO_4$. What is the role of these reagents?
options: They act as Lewis acid catalysts that polarise $I_2$
They oxidise the HI formed, so the reversible reaction is driven forward
They nitrate the ring first, which activates it towards iodine
They convert iodobenzene into a diazonium salt
questions.explanation:
Direct iodination of arenes is reversible. The HI produced can reduce iodobenzene back to benzene.
$HNO_3$ or $HIO_4$ oxidises HI as it forms. This removes a product and shifts the equilibrium towards iodobenzene.
They are not Lewis acid catalysts; that role belongs to Fe or $FeCl_3$ in chlorination and bromination.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of common name and IUPAC name is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: number from the end nearest the double bond, which places Br on C-3 of propene.
(2) Correct: in IUPAC, benzyl chloride is named as a methane carrying phenyl and chloro groups.
(3) Incorrect: CH2=CHCl contains a C=C bond, so it is chloroethene. Chloroethane is CH3CH2Cl.
(4) Correct: F is on C-1 of propane.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (name of reaction) with List-II (reaction).
List-I
(A) Finkelstein reaction
(B) Swarts reaction
(C) Sandmeyer reaction
(D) Wurtz–Fittig reaction
List-II
(i) Benzenediazonium chloride + $Cu_2Cl_2$ → chlorobenzene
(ii) Alkyl halide + aryl halide + Na in dry ether → alkylarene
(iii) R–Cl + NaI in dry acetone → R–I
(iv) R–Br + AgF on heating → R–F
questions.explanation:
A-iii: The Finkelstein reaction is halogen exchange with NaI in dry acetone. NaCl/NaBr precipitates and drives the reaction forward.
B-iv: The Swarts reaction uses a metallic fluoride such as AgF, $Hg_2F_2$, $CoF_2$ or $SbF_3$ to make alkyl fluorides.
C-i: In the Sandmeyer reaction, CuCl or CuBr replaces the diazonium group with –Cl or –Br.
D-ii: In the Wurtz–Fittig reaction, alkyl and aryl halides couple with Na in dry ether to give an alkylarene.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many structural isomers of the formula C4H8Cl2 are vicinal (vic) dihalides, i.e., compounds in the common system that would be named as alkylene dihalides?
questions.explanation:
Vic-dihalides carry the two Cl atoms on adjacent carbons.
n-Butane skeleton: 1,2-dichlorobutane and 2,3-dichlorobutane. 3,4- is the same compound as 1,2-.
Isobutane skeleton: only C-1 and C-2 are adjacent, which gives 1,2-dichloro-2-methylpropane.
Total vic isomers = 3. The 1,3-, 1,4- and gem isomers are excluded.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following methyl halides reacts fastest with aqueous $OH^-$ by the $S_N2$ mechanism?
questions.explanation:
For the same alkyl group, the reactivity of R–X in both $S_N1$ and $S_N2$ follows R–I > R–Br > R–Cl >> R–F.
Iodine is the largest halogen, so the C–I bond is the longest and weakest (bond enthalpy 234 kJ/mol).
Iodide is therefore the best leaving group.
$CH_3F$ has the strongest C–X bond and is the least reactive.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Heating methyl bromide with Hg$_2$F$_2$ gives methyl fluoride. This halogen-exchange reaction is called:
questions.explanation:
Swarts reaction makes alkyl fluorides. An alkyl chloride or bromide is heated with a metallic fluoride such as AgF, Hg$_2$F$_2$, CoF$_2$ or SbF$_3$.
Finkelstein reaction is also a halogen exchange, but it uses NaI in dry acetone and gives alkyl iodides.
Sandmeyer reaction gives aryl halides from diazonium salts.
Wurtz reaction couples alkyl halides with Na.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct IUPAC name of neo-pentyl bromide, $(CH_3)_3CCH_2Br$, is:
questions.explanation:
The longest chain that contains the C–Br carbon has 3 carbons, so the parent is propane.
Number the chain from the $CH_2Br$ end. Br is then on C-1 and two methyl groups are on C-2.
The name is therefore 1-Bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane.
2-Bromo-2-methylpropane is a different compound, tert-butyl bromide $(CH_3)_3CBr$, which has only 4 carbons.
1-Bromopentane is the straight-chain isomer.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The two enantiomers of butan-2-ol differ from each other in their
options: direction of rotation of plane polarised light
questions.explanation:
Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images.
They have identical physical properties such as melting point, boiling point and refractive index.
They differ only in the direction in which they rotate plane polarised light. One is dextrorotatory and the other is laevorotatory, by an equal angle.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 2-Methylbutane, $(CH_3)_2CHCH_2CH_3$, undergoes free radical monochlorination. How many of the monochloro structural isomers formed contain a chiral (asymmetric) carbon atom?
questions.explanation:
Four structural isomers are formed:
(i) 1-chloro-3-methylbutane: no carbon has four different groups, so achiral.
(ii) 2-chloro-3-methylbutane: C-2 carries H, Cl, $CH_3$ and isopropyl, so chiral.
(iii) 2-chloro-2-methylbutane: C-2 carries two $CH_3$ groups, so achiral.
(iv) 1-chloro-2-methylbutane: C-2 carries H, $CH_3$, $CH_2Cl$ and $C_2H_5$, so chiral.
Two isomers are chiral.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In which of the following halides is the halogen atom bonded to an $sp^2$-hybridised carbon atom?
questions.explanation:
In vinylic halides the halogen sits directly on a carbon of the C=C double bond, so that carbon is $sp^2$.
CH2=CHCl (vinyl chloride) is vinylic, so it has an $sp^2$ C–Cl bond.
CH2=CHCH2Cl is allylic and C6H5CH2Cl is benzylic. In both, Cl is on an $sp^3$ carbon next to the C=C or the ring.
(CH3)3CCl is a tertiary alkyl halide with an $sp^3$ carbon.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (polyhalogen compound) with List-II (property or use):
List-I
(a) Chloroform
(b) Iodoform
(c) Freon 12
(d) DDT
List-II
(i) Its antiseptic action is due to liberation of free iodine
(ii) Slowly oxidised by air in light to phosgene, so it is stored in dark, completely filled bottles
(iii) Not metabolised rapidly and gets stored in fatty tissues of animals
(iv) Manufactured from tetrachloromethane by the Swarts reaction and used in refrigeration
questions.explanation:
(a)-(ii): $CHCl_3$ is slowly oxidised by air in light to poisonous phosgene ($COCl_2$). It is therefore kept in dark bottles filled to the top to exclude air.
(b)-(i): the antiseptic action of $CHI_3$ comes from the free iodine it releases, not from iodoform itself.
(c)-(iv): $CCl_2F_2$ (Freon 12) is made from $CCl_4$ by the Swarts reaction and is used as a refrigerant.
(d)-(iii): DDT is chemically stable and fat-soluble, so it accumulates in fatty tissue.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): 1-Chloro-3-nitrobenzene undergoes hydrolysis with aqueous NaOH about as sluggishly as chlorobenzene, whereas 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene reacts much more easily.
Reason (R): When $OH^-$ attacks the meta isomer, none of the resonance structures of the carbanion carry the negative charge on the carbon bearing the $-NO_2$ group.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: a nitro group at the o/p position speeds up nucleophilic substitution, but at the meta position it has no effect on reactivity.
R is true: in the carbanion formed by $OH^-$ attack, the negative charge appears at positions ortho and para to the halogen.
For the meta isomer, these positions never coincide with the carbon carrying $-NO_2$, so the nitro group cannot stabilise the charge.
This is exactly why the meta isomer is not activated, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reagent reacting with a haloalkane R–X) with List-II (main organic product).
List-I
(A) KCN
(B) AgCN
(C) $KNO_2$
(D) $AgNO_2$
List-II
(i) R–$NO_2$
(ii) R–NC
(iii) R–CN
(iv) R–O–N=O
questions.explanation:
Cyanide and nitrite are ambident nucleophiles, so each can attack through two different atoms.
A-iii: KCN is ionic, so the attack occurs through carbon and gives a nitrile, R–CN.
B-ii: AgCN is largely covalent, so nitrogen donates its lone pair and gives an isocyanide, R–NC.
C-iv: $KNO_2$ attacks through oxygen and gives an alkyl nitrite.
D-i: $AgNO_2$ attacks through nitrogen and gives a nitroalkane.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the SN1 reaction of alkyl halides are correct?
(i) The rate depends only on the concentration of the alkyl halide.
(ii) The carbocation intermediate is $sp^2$ hybridised and planar.
(iii) An optically active alkyl halide gives a racemic product.
(iv) It is generally carried out in polar protic solvents such as water or alcohol.
(v) Methyl bromide reacts faster than tert-butyl bromide by this mechanism.
(vi) The carbocation-forming step is fast and irreversible.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct. The slow step involves only R–X, so the reaction is first order.
(ii) Correct. The carbocation is $sp^2$ hybridised, planar and achiral.
(iii) Correct. The nucleophile can attack from either face of the planar carbocation, so racemisation occurs.
(iv) Correct. Polar protic solvents solvate the halide ion and help the C–X bond break.
(v) Incorrect. A 3° carbocation is far more stable, so tert-butyl bromide reacts faster.
(vi) Incorrect. Step I is the slow and reversible step.
Correct statements = 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction between $CH_3Cl$ and hydroxide ion to give methanol follows the $S_N2$ mechanism. Which rate expression is correct for it?
questions.explanation:
$S_N2$ means bimolecular nucleophilic substitution.
Bond formation (C–OH) and bond breaking (C–Cl) happen together in a single step. So both reactants take part in the rate-determining step.
The reaction is therefore second order: first order in $CH_3Cl$ and first order in $OH^-$.
Rate = $k[CH_3Cl]$ is the first-order expression typical of $S_N1$, so it does not apply here.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Hydrolysis of optically active 2-bromobutane by the SN1 mechanism gives (±)-butan-2-ol.
Reason (R): The carbocation formed in the slow step is sp2 hybridised and planar, so the nucleophile can attack it from either face.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: SN1 hydrolysis of optically active 2-bromobutane gives the racemic product (±)-butan-2-ol.
R is true: the carbocation is sp2 hybridised and planar, which makes it achiral.
Attack from the face where Br was gives one configuration. Attack from the opposite face gives the other.
This produces both enantiomers, which explains the racemisation. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): When an alkyl halide having $\beta$-hydrogens is treated with a bulky base, elimination is favoured over substitution.
Reason (R): A bulky species finds it sterically difficult to approach the tetravalent carbon, so it prefers to abstract a $\beta$-proton instead.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Substitution and elimination compete with each other, and the size of the base or nucleophile is one factor that decides which route is taken.
R is true. A bulky reagent cannot easily reach the crowded carbon bearing the halogen. A $\beta$-hydrogen on the periphery of the molecule is far more accessible.
R therefore explains why elimination wins in this case.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is an allylic halide?
questions.explanation:
An allylic halide has the halogen on an $sp^3$ carbon that is next to a C=C double bond.
In $CH_2=CHCH_2Br$ (allyl bromide), Br sits on the $CH_2$ group next to the double bond, so it is allylic.
$CH_2=CHBr$ is vinylic, because Br is on an $sp^2$ carbon of the C=C.
$C_6H_5Br$ is an aryl halide.
$C_6H_5CH_2Br$ is benzylic. Its $sp^3$ carbon is attached to an aromatic ring, not to an isolated C=C.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following, on reacting with $CH_3MgBr$, will convert it into methane?
Water, ethanol, ethylamine ($CH_3CH_2NH_2$), diethyl ether, n-hexane
questions.explanation:
Grignard reagents react with any source of a proton and give the hydrocarbon.
Water: yes, it has an acidic O–H.
Ethanol: yes, it has an O–H.
Ethylamine: yes. NCERT states that amines (with N–H) are acidic enough to react.
Diethyl ether: no. It has no acidic H and is the solvent in which RMgX is prepared.
n-Hexane: no. It has no acidic H.
So 3 of these give methane.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (compound) with List-II (use or property described in NCERT).
List-I
(A) Freon 12 ($CCl_2F_2$)
(B) Iodoform
(C) DDT
(D) Halothane
List-II
(i) Its antiseptic action comes from the free iodine it liberates
(ii) Anaesthetic used during surgery
(iii) Made from tetrachloromethane by the Swarts reaction
(iv) Fat-soluble, so it is stored in fatty tissues of animals and builds up over time
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(A) Freon 12 matches (iii): NCERT states it is manufactured from $CCl_4$ by the Swarts reaction, using metallic fluorides.
(B) Iodoform matches (i): its antiseptic property is due to the iodine it liberates, not to iodoform itself.
(C) DDT matches (iv): it is chemically stable and fat soluble, is not metabolised quickly and so accumulates in fatty tissues.
(D) Halothane matches (ii): it is a synthetic halogen compound used as an anaesthetic.
Option (2) is wrong because it gives the anaesthetic role to iodoform.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the Finkelstein reaction, CH$_3$CH$_2$Br + NaI → CH$_3$CH$_2$I + NaBr is carried out in dry acetone. Why does the reaction go almost to completion?
options: NaI is insoluble in acetone and is removed as it reacts
Acetone reacts with HBr formed and removes it
NaBr formed precipitates in dry acetone, which shifts the equilibrium forward (Le Chatelier's principle)
Iodide is a poorer nucleophile than bromide in acetone
questions.explanation:
NaI dissolves in dry acetone, but NaCl and NaBr do not.
As NaBr precipitates, a product is removed from the solution, so the equilibrium shifts to the right by Le Chatelier's principle.
No HBr is formed in this reaction.
It is the precipitation of NaBr, not the solubility of NaI, that drives the reaction.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chloroform is stored in closed, dark coloured bottles that are filled completely to the top. The main reason for this precaution is that chloroform:
options: is slowly oxidised by air in the presence of light to the highly poisonous gas phosgene ($COCl_2$)
decomposes in light to give free iodine, which stains the bottle
absorbs moisture from air and is hydrolysed to methanol
is highly flammable and catches fire when exposed to sunlight
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: in the presence of light, air slowly oxidises chloroform to carbonyl chloride, also called phosgene, which is extremely poisonous.
Dark bottles keep light out. Filling the bottle completely leaves no room for air, so the oxygen needed for the oxidation is excluded.
Option (2) wrongly applies the iodine-liberation idea, which belongs to iodoform, not chloroform.
Options (3) and (4) describe problems that NCERT does not give as the reason for this storage method.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following compounds are denser than water?
$n$-$C_3H_7Cl$, $n$-$C_3H_7Br$, $n$-$C_3H_7I$, $CH_2Cl_2$, $CHCl_3$, $CCl_4$
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that bromo, iodo and polychloro derivatives are heavier than water. Water has a density of 1 g/mL.
$n$-$C_3H_7Cl$ (0.89 g/mL) is a monochloro compound and is lighter than water.
$n$-$C_3H_7Br$ (1.335), $n$-$C_3H_7I$ (1.747), $CH_2Cl_2$ (1.336), $CHCl_3$ (1.489) and $CCl_4$ (1.595) are all denser than water.
So the count is 5.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Propan-2-ol is optically inactive.
Reason (R): The central carbon of propan-2-ol carries two identical methyl groups, so the molecule is superimposable on its mirror image.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Propan-2-ol is achiral, so it does not rotate plane polarised light.
R is true. The central carbon carries H, OH and two CH$_3$ groups, so it is not an asymmetric carbon.
If the mirror image is rotated by 180°, it overlaps the original molecule completely.
Superimposability on the mirror image means the molecule is achiral and therefore optically inactive, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In 1-bromopropane, $CH_3CH_2CH_2Br$, how many β-hydrogen atoms can be removed during β-elimination with alcoholic KOH?
questions.explanation:
The α-carbon is the carbon that carries the halogen. Here it is the $CH_2Br$ carbon.
The β-carbon is the carbon next to the α-carbon. Here it is the middle $CH_2$ group.
The β-carbon carries 2 hydrogen atoms. These are the hydrogens lost in β-elimination, which gives propene.
The terminal $CH_3$ is a γ-carbon, so its 3 H are not counted. Option 3 wrongly includes them.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): 1-Chloro-3-nitrobenzene is not noticeably more reactive than chlorobenzene towards hydroxide ion.
Reason (R): When $OH^-$ attacks the carbon bearing Cl in 1-chloro-3-nitrobenzene, none of the resonance structures of the carbanion place the negative charge on the carbon bearing the $-NO_2$ group.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that an $-NO_2$ group at the meta position has no effect on the reactivity of a haloarene.
R is true. In the carbanion, the negative charge appears only at positions ortho and para to the carbon attacked. A meta $-NO_2$ group never carries this charge.
So the nitro group cannot stabilise the carbanion, and the rate is not increased. R therefore explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Freon 12 ($CCl_2F_2$) is manufactured from tetrachloromethane by heating it with a metallic fluoride. This halogen exchange reaction is known as:
questions.explanation:
Swarts reaction makes alkyl fluorides by heating an alkyl chloride or bromide with a metallic fluoride such as $AgF$, $Hg_2F_2$, $CoF_2$ or $SbF_3$. NCERT states that Freon 12 is made from $CCl_4$ by this reaction.
Finkelstein reaction is also a halogen exchange, but it uses NaI in dry acetone and gives iodides, not fluorides.
Sandmeyer's reaction uses diazonium salts.
Wurtz reaction couples alkyl halides using Na.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Among the methyl halides, which one has the highest dipole moment?
questions.explanation:
NCERT dipole moments: $CH_3F$ 1.847 D, $CH_3Cl$ 1.860 D, $CH_3Br$ 1.830 D, $CH_3I$ 1.636 D.
Dipole moment depends on both the charge separation and the bond length.
In $CH_3Cl$, the fairly large charge separation combined with a longer bond than C–F gives the maximum value.
$CH_3F$ is the tempting choice because F is the most electronegative halogen, but its very short bond lowers its dipole moment.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Bromobenzene is treated with sodium metal in dry ether. What is the organic product, and what is the reaction called?
questions.explanation:
Aryl halides treated with sodium in dry ether join two aryl groups together.
So two phenyl groups couple to give biphenyl ($C_6H_5$–$C_6H_5$). This is the Fittig reaction.
The Wurtz–Fittig reaction needs a mixture of an alkyl halide and an aryl halide; it gives an alkylarene such as toluene.
A Grignard reagent forms with Mg, not Na.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A freshly prepared solution of benzenediazonium chloride is shaken with an aqueous solution of a reagent X, and iodobenzene is formed. No cuprous salt is required. X is:
questions.explanation:
Chloro and bromo groups are introduced by Sandmeyer's reaction, which uses CuCl or CuBr.
NCERT notes that replacing the diazonium group by iodine needs no cuprous halide. The diazonium salt is simply shaken with potassium iodide.
NaI in dry acetone is the Finkelstein reaction, which applies to alkyl halides, not diazonium salts.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the halides $CH_3I$, $CH_3Cl$, $(CH_3)_3CI$ and $(CH_3)_3CCl$. Which pair correctly identifies the compound reacting fastest by $S_N1$ and the compound reacting fastest by $S_N2$, respectively?
questions.explanation:
Structure effect: $S_N1$ needs a stable carbocation, so the tertiary halides react faster. $S_N2$ needs little steric hindrance, so the methyl halides react faster.
Leaving group effect: in both mechanisms, R–I > R–Br > R–Cl. The larger iodide leaves most easily.
Fastest $S_N1$ is therefore the tertiary iodide, $(CH_3)_3CI$.
Fastest $S_N2$ is the methyl iodide, $CH_3I$.
Options with chlorides ignore the leaving-group effect.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements correctly explain why chlorobenzene is much less reactive than chloroalkanes towards nucleophilic substitution?
(i) The lone pairs of Cl are in conjugation with the ring, which gives the C–Cl bond partial double bond character.
(ii) The carbon bearing Cl is $sp^2$ hybridised and holds the C–Cl bonding pair tightly.
(iii) The phenyl cation formed by self-ionisation is well stabilised by resonance, which favours an $S_N1$ path.
(iv) An electron-rich nucleophile is repelled as it approaches the electron-rich aromatic ring.
(v) An $-NO_2$ group at the meta position activates the ring as strongly as one at the para position.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: resonance makes C–Cl cleavage difficult.
(ii) Correct: the $sp^2$ carbon has more s-character, so the C–Cl bond is shorter and stronger.
(iii) Incorrect: the phenyl cation is NOT resonance stabilised, so the $S_N1$ path is ruled out.
(iv) Correct: there is repulsion between the nucleophile and the π-electron cloud.
(v) Incorrect, and in any case not a reason for low reactivity: a meta $-NO_2$ group has no activating effect.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorobenzene is nitrated with a mixture of concentrated $HNO_3$ and concentrated $H_2SO_4$. What are the major products?
questions.explanation:
Halogen on a benzene ring is ortho/para directing, even though it is slightly deactivating.
So the nitro group enters ortho and para to Cl, giving 1-chloro-2-nitrobenzene and 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene (the para isomer is major).
The meta product is not the major product, because resonance increases electron density mainly at the o and p positions.
The C–Cl bond is not replaced in this electrophilic reaction.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Arrange the following primary bromides in decreasing order of reactivity towards $S_N2$ displacement by $OH^-$:
(P) $CH_3CH_2CH_2Br$
(Q) $(CH_3)_2CHCH_2Br$
(R) $(CH_3)_3CCH_2Br$
questions.explanation:
In $S_N2$, the nucleophile must approach the carbon bearing Br from the back side.
Bulky groups on or near this carbon hinder that approach.
All three compounds are 1° bromides, so compare branching at the adjacent (β) carbon.
P has no branch, Q has one methyl branch, and R (neopentyl bromide) has three methyls.
Steric hindrance increases P < Q < R, so reactivity is P > Q > R.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorobenzene is nitrated with a mixture of concentrated $HNO_3$ and $H_2SO_4$. Which products are formed as the major products?
options: Nitrobenzene, by replacement of Cl with $NO_2$
questions.explanation:
The halogen atom is slightly deactivating but ortho/para directing in electrophilic substitution.
Resonance raises the electron density at the ortho and para positions. So the nitro group enters there, giving 1-chloro-2-nitrobenzene and 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene (the para isomer is the major one).
The meta product is not the main product.
The Cl atom is not replaced, because this is substitution of ring hydrogen by an electrophile.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the study of optical activity, which instrument is used to measure the angle through which the plane of plane polarised light is rotated by a solution of a compound?
questions.explanation:
A Nicol prism converts ordinary light into plane polarised light. It does not measure rotation.
When this light passes through a solution of an optically active compound, its plane is rotated.
The angle of rotation is measured with a polarimeter.
The Nicol prism is the tempting wrong choice because it is part of the same set-up, but it only produces the polarised light.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Bromoethane is heated with a metallic fluoride to prepare fluoroethane by the Swarts reaction. Which of the following reagents is NOT used for this purpose?
questions.explanation:
The Swarts reaction makes alkyl fluorides by heating an alkyl chloride or bromide with a metallic fluoride such as $AgF$, $Hg_2F_2$, $CoF_2$ or $SbF_3$.
NaI in dry acetone is the reagent for the Finkelstein reaction. It gives alkyl iodides, not fluorides.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The IUPAC name of neo-pentyl bromide, (CH3)3CCH2Br, is:
questions.explanation:
Pick the longest chain that contains the C bearing Br: CH2Br–C(CH3)2–CH3. That is three carbons, so the parent is propane.
Numbering from the CH2Br end puts Br on C-1 and two methyl groups on C-2.
The name is therefore 1-bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane.
2-Bromo-2-methylbutane is a different isomer, (CH3)2CBrCH2CH3, which is tertiary.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The C–Cl bond length is about 169 pm in chlorobenzene but about 177 pm in a chloroalkane. Which reason given in NCERT explains this shorter bond?
options: The carbon bonded to Cl in chlorobenzene is $sp^2$ hybridised. Its greater s-character makes it more electronegative, so it holds the bonding pair more tightly.
The chlorine atom in chlorobenzene is smaller than the chlorine atom in a chloroalkane.
The carbon bonded to Cl in chlorobenzene is $sp^3$ hybridised and has less s-character.
Chlorobenzene readily forms a resonance-stabilised phenyl cation.
questions.explanation:
In a haloarene, the C–X carbon is $sp^2$ hybridised. In a haloalkane, it is $sp^3$ hybridised.
Greater s-character makes the carbon more electronegative, so it holds the C–Cl electron pair more tightly. This shortens the bond. Resonance also adds partial double bond character.
The size of the chlorine atom is the same in both compounds.
The phenyl cation is not resonance stabilised.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (reagent reacting with an alkyl halide R–X) with List-II (main product).
List-I:
(A) KCN
(B) AgCN
(C) $KNO_2$
(D) $CH_3COOAg$
List-II:
(I) R–O–N=O
(II) R–NC
(III) $CH_3COOR$
(IV) R–CN
questions.explanation:
(A) KCN is ionic. Free $CN^-$ attacks through carbon, giving the nitrile R–CN (IV).
(B) AgCN is covalent. Nitrogen donates its lone pair, giving the isocyanide R–NC (II).
(C) $KNO_2$ attacks through oxygen, giving the alkyl nitrite R–O–N=O (I).
(D) The silver carboxylate gives the ester $CH_3COOR$ (III).
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 6 · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (compound) with List-II (type of halide):
List-I
(a) CH2=CHCH2Br
(b) C6H5CH2Br
(c) CH2=CHBr
(d) C6H5Br
List-II
(i) Vinylic halide
(ii) Aryl halide
(iii) Allylic halide
(iv) Benzylic halide
questions.explanation:
(a) Br is on an $sp^3$ CH2 next to C=C, so it is allylic (iii).
(b) Br is on an $sp^3$ CH2 attached to a benzene ring, so it is benzylic (iv).
(c) Br is on an $sp^2$ carbon of C=C, so it is vinylic (i).
(d) Br is directly on an $sp^2$ ring carbon, so it is an aryl halide (ii).
Answer: (1)
